preconditions.description: Attacker must be the owner of the contract
Contract must hold NFT tokens that can be withdrawn

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call the withdrawNft function with: (1) token_ parameter set to the NFT contract address, (2) destination_ parameter set to attacker's address, (3) tokenId_ parameter set to the specific NFT token ID to withdraw. The owner can extract any NFT held by the contract regardless of who originally deposited it.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CUSD contract inherits from Withdrawable which has a withdrawNft function that allows the owner to withdraw ANY NFT held by the contract. The function only checks that the destination is not zero and that the caller is the owner. There's no validation that the NFT was deposited by the owner or that they have legitimate rights to withdraw it. This is a classic owner privilege abuse vulnerability.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(). 2. Call withdrawNft with the NFT token address, attacker's address as destination, and a valid token ID. 3. The NFT will be transferred from the contract to the attacker, increasing their balance.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the owner address of the target contract. 2. Use vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate the owner. 3. Call withdrawNft(tokenAddress, attacker, tokenId). 4. Stop the prank. 5. Verify the attacker's NFT balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The withdrawNft vulnerability is real, but the test environment doesn't have a valid NFT contract set up. I need to create a mock ERC721 contract using vm.etch, then have the target contract hold an NFT from it, and finally withdraw it.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Create a minimal ERC721 mock contract bytecode and deploy it using vm.etch. 2. Set up the mock NFT so the target contract owns token ID 1. 3. Impersonate the owner and call withdrawNft to extract the NFT to attacker's address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.etch to deploy a minimal ERC721 contract at a known address. 2. Use vm.store to set the target contract as the owner of token ID 1 in the mock NFT. 3. Impersonate the contract owner. 4. Call withdrawNft with the mock NFT address. 5. Verify the attacker now owns the NFT.
